# ColdChain AI - ML (ml/)

Machine-learning pipeline for spoilage risk prediction, forecasting, anomaly
detection and image classification.

## DATASET NOTICE (read this first)

There is **no real-world dataset** in this repository. The training data is
**SYNTHETIC / DEMO DATA** generated by `ml/data/generate_raw_dataset.py`
(simulated shipments: sensor noise, door events, GPS routes, cooling failures).

* Raw data: `data/raw/coldchain_synthetic_v1.csv` (generated, git-ignored)
* Processed data: `data/processed/{train,val,test}.csv` + `metadata.json`
* **All metrics reported from this data are DEVELOPMENT/DEMO metrics only.
  They are NOT real-world validation and must not be presented as such.**
* The 17 PostgreSQL telemetry rows from Steps 2-3 are live demo/operational
  data only - they are not used as an ML training dataset.
* CNN images: `ml/data/images/` contains clearly-marked **DEMO** procedural
  images (`demo_*.png` + `DEMO_DATA.md`). Replace with real labeled photos
  (`train/<class>/`, `val/<class>/`) for real validation.

## Directory structure

    ml/
      data/
        generate_raw_dataset.py   # creates the SYNTHETIC raw dataset (data/raw/)
        prepare_data.py           # validation, features, labels, chronological split
        images/                   # CNN images (train/, val/ per class, DEMO only)
      utils/
        features.py               # past-only features (reuses backend exposure engine)
        common.py                 # split, scaling, metrics, artifacts, windows, AE fns
      training/
        train_xgboost.py          # tabular spoilage-risk model
        train_lstm.py             # temperature/humidity forecasting
        train_autoencoder.py      # anomaly detection on normal windows
        train_cnn.py              # packaging-condition image classifier
        explain_xgboost.py        # SHAP explanations
      tests/
        test_ml.py                # leakage, split, models, artifacts, SHAP tests
      artifacts/                  # saved models, metrics, SHAP outputs (git-ignored)
      requirements.txt

## Data-preparation pipeline (preventing leakage)

1. Read raw CSV - never modify `data/raw/`.
2. Validate columns, drop missing temperatures, reject duplicate
   `shipment_id + timestamp` rows.
3. Build features with `ml/utils/features.py`. Every feature at row `t`
   uses only readings `<= t`: cumulative exposure computed by the **backend
   engine** (`backend/app/services/exposure.py`, shared - not duplicated),
   rolling stats of the past, distance travelled so far, door events so far.
4. Label `future_discard` uses the FUTURE (spoil event within the next 24
   readings). Future data appears only in the label, never in a feature.
5. Group-chronological 70/15/15 split by shipment start time: time order is
   preserved and no shipment appears in two splits (no group leakage).
6. Imputation/scaler statistics are fitted on the TRAIN split only.
7. Saves `data/processed/train.csv`, `val.csv`, `test.csv`, `metadata.json`.

## Model training

| Model | Script | Input | Output / artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| XGBoost | `ml/training/train_xgboost.py` | engineered features | `xgboost_spoilage.ubj`, `xgboost_features.json` |
| LSTM | `ml/training/train_lstm.py` | 48-reading windows of temperature+humidity | `lstm_forecast.keras`, `lstm_scaler.pkl`, `lstm_meta.json` |
| Autoencoder | `ml/training/train_autoencoder.py` | 24-reading normal windows | `autoencoder.keras`, `autoencoder_meta.json` |
| CNN | `ml/training/train_cnn.py` | 96x96 RGB packaging images | `cnn_packaging.keras`, `cnn_meta.json` |
| SHAP | `ml/training/explain_xgboost.py` | XGBoost model + test rows | `shap_importance.json`, `shap_explanations.json` |

Class imbalance strategy (XGBoost): `scale_pos_weight = n_negative / n_positive`,
`eval_metric=aucpr`, and a decision threshold tuned on the VALIDATION split
(never the test split). Because positives are rare, precision/recall/F1 and
PR-AUC are reported alongside accuracy and the majority-class baseline.

Autoencoder inference (reusable functions):

    from ml.utils.common import reconstruction_error, is_anomaly
    errors = reconstruction_error(model, X)          # per-sample error
    flags = is_anomaly(model, X, threshold)          # True = anomaly

## Running the pipeline

Run from the project root with the backend virtual environment active:

    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\data\generate_raw_dataset.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\data\prepare_data.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\training\train_xgboost.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\training\train_lstm.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\training\train_autoencoder.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\training\train_cnn.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python ml\training\explain_xgboost.py
    backend\.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest ml/tests -q

Dependencies: `pip install -r ml/requirements.txt` (CPU-only TensorFlow).

## Interpretation (SHAP)

`explain_xgboost.py` uses `shap.TreeExplainer`:

* Global importance: mean absolute SHAP value per feature.
* Per-prediction: the top factors that increased or decreased spoilage risk
  for each explained row, in a UI-ready structure.

## Known limitations

* Synthetic data: models learn simulated physics; metrics do not transfer.
* Only ~400 shipments x 96 readings; LSTM/CNN results are pipeline checks,
  not research-grade benchmarks.
* CNN has no real labeled images yet - demo images only.
* No temporal CV: a single chronological split is used for simplicity.
